prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep safety authority). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; optional Passenger Misconnect Count); these reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Gate Conflict Detector; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine grants emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time); Aircraft Operator Representative (submits Flight Intent Messages, challenges via Decision Log); Regional Flow Manager (RFM); Slot Coordinator; Data Governance Steward; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Airport Duty Manager (ADM; Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor; System Support Engineer; Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Network Operations Liaison; Airspace Sector Planner; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator. Training: recurrent, simulations of all mode transitions, deviations logged in Decision Log; confirmations for high-impact actions, no silent mode changes. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance State; Contingency Fallback State (ADM declares after consulting RFM). Deployment: Readiness Gate 2: Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Weather Ingest Gateway connect non-disruptively; Gate 3: local procedures mapped to Portal, Sequence Manager, Ramp Board, DMS, Arrival Console; Gate 4: training, shadow ops, contingency, acceptance done before live decisions. Interface certification separate from operational acceptance; tests structure, timestamps, identity, replay, duplicates, outage recovery, degraded rejection. DPS, CAM, SAE, Gate Conflict Detector, Sector Load

New part:
S909: Expansion beyond the pilot airports shall occur in waves that group airports by interface maturity, traffic dependency, stakeholder readiness, and available support capacity.
S910: Each onboarding wave shall include a stabilization period in which the System Support Engineer and Data Governance Steward monitor defect trends, data quality, access changes, and user adoption.
S911: Full regional deployment shall be declared only after the Regional Flow Manager confirms that operational benefits, safety constraints, cyber controls, and stakeholder obligations remain stable across multiple airports and traffic conditions.
S912: Operational service management for the Regional Flow Platform shall begin when a deployed airport is accepted into steady state support after the regional stabilization period.
S913: The service model shall distinguish continuous operational support from planned engineering support so that safety related traffic flow functions remain protected at all times.
S914: The System Support Engineer shall provide round the clock on call coverage for production incidents affecting the Regional Flow Platform, Airport CDM Portal, Slot Allocation Engine, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, and Alert Distribution Hub.
S915: Standard service desk coverage for access requests, reporting questions, configuration inquiries, and minor usability issues shall be available during normal regional administrative hours on business days.
S916: During published peak traffic periods, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, and Recovery Phase, the on call support posture shall be raised so that the System Support Engineer can join the Digital Briefing Room without delay.
S917: The Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, and Network Operations Liaison shall retain operational command authority during support activity.
S918: The System Support Engineer shall advise operational supervisors on technical status, known workarounds, data integrity concerns, and recovery options, but shall not issue traffic management instructions.
S919: Incidents shall be classified by operational effect, with the highest priority assigned to loss of common situational awareness, loss of slot computation, corruption of operational timing data, or failure of alert distribution during active traffic management.
S920: A critical incident shall be acknowledged within fifteen minutes and shall have continuous technical ownership until service is restored or an agreed operational workaround is in place.
S921: A high priority incident that degrades a major function without stopping tactical coordination shall be acknowledged within thirty minutes and shall be reviewed with the affected operational supervisor at least hourly.
S922: Medium and low priority incidents shall be handled through the service queue, with target updates provided at intervals appropriate to their operational impact and planned resolution path.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
